esop.source: Customer declaration · MCA filings · SEBI DRHP registry · secondary-market price feed

holdings.headline: 4,800 vested options · indicative ₹61.2L on listing

news.headline: Helix Logistics files DRHP for a ₹1,450 Cr IPO
news.detail: Fresh issue of ₹900 Cr and an offer for sale of ₹550 Cr. Indicative price band of ₹1,240–1,310 reported by two merchant bankers; listing expected in the December quarter.

news.headline: Unlisted shares trading at ₹1,180 in the grey market
news.detail: Up from ₹840 six months ago. Employee sell-side liquidity has been thin since the company restricted transfers ahead of the filing.

holdings.detail: She holds 4,800 vested but unexercised options from her years at Helix, at a strike of ₹42. Exercising costs ₹2.02L. At the mid point of the reported band those shares are worth about ₹61.2L, a gain of ₹59.2L. Tax lands in two places: the spread at exercise is taxed as a perquisite at slab — roughly ₹18.4L — and anything gained after listing is capital gains. The perquisite is due whether or not she sells, which is exactly the cash-flow problem an ESOP funding facility exists to solve.

opportunities.title: ESOP funding facility
opportunities.why: Covers the ₹2.02L exercise cost and the ₹18.4L perquisite tax so she does not have to sell into the listing to pay the tax bill.
opportunities.prompt: Work out an ESOP funding facility for Vandana Singh: 4,800 Helix Logistics options at a ₹42 strike, ₹18.4L perquisite tax, listing expected in the December quarter. Show the facility size, tenor and exit route.

opportunities.title: 3-in-1 demat and trading account
opportunities.why: Allotment needs a demat account in her name before the exercise window closes. She does not hold one with IDBI today.
opportunities.prompt: Explain what Vandana Singh needs to open a 3-in-1 IDBI demat and trading account before her Helix Logistics options are allotted, and how long it takes.

opportunities.title: Post-listing wealth mandate
opportunities.why: A liquidity event of this size usually moves to a competitor within weeks of credit. Booking the conversation now is the difference between a deposit and a mandate.
opportunities.prompt: Draft a plan for deploying a ₹59.2L post-listing inflow for Vandana Singh, age 54, self-employed, covering capital-gains treatment, liquid parking and a staggered allocation.

holdings.headline: 1,200 options · 600 vested · no live event
holdings.detail: A small advisory grant with no liquidity event in sight and no secondary market. Worth recording because it sits on her net-worth statement and affects how much of the Helix proceeds she can afford to lock up, but there is nothing to sell against it today.

opportunities.title: Record in net-worth statement
opportunities.why: Keeps the wealth profile complete ahead of the Helix conversation. No action needed from the customer.
opportunities.prompt: Add Vandana Singh's 600 vested Saanvi Analytics options at a ₹340 last valuation to her net-worth view and explain why it is illiquid.

credit.source: Soft bureau pull · CIBIL TransUnion, 16 Sep 2026 · no score impact

signals.title: Two credit-card enquiries at other banks in 90 days
signals.headline: HDFC Bank on 22 Aug, Axis Bank on 05 Sep
signals.detail: She is shopping for a credit card right now and has not come to us, which is the honest read of two card enquiries in three weeks at two private banks. Neither has converted yet — the bureau shows no new card account — so the window is open. She has banked with IDBI for eight years and holds four accounts, and we have never put a card in front of her.
signals.opportunity: Pre-approved IDBI card at ₹4.25L, above what either enquiry is likely to sanction on income proof alone, issued against internal banking history rather than a fresh bureau pull.
signals.prompt: Vandana Singh has two external credit-card enquiries in the last 90 days and no IDBI card. Check her pre-approved card eligibility and draft what I should say when I call her.

signals.title: External card running at 71% utilisation
signals.headline: ₹1.78L drawn on a ₹2.50L limit, never late
signals.detail: Utilisation above 30% drags a bureau score even when every payment is on time, and hers has been sitting in the 60–75% band for five months. That is a business owner using a personal card for stock purchases because the working-capital limit is tight — the same story as the working-capital enquiry already open on her file.
signals.opportunity: A balance transfer onto an IDBI card at 0.99% for 6 months clears ₹1.78L of revolving interest, and the higher limit drops her utilisation ratio to about 42%, which the bureau will read as an improvement within two cycles.
signals.prompt: Model a balance transfer of ₹1.78L from Vandana Singh's SBI Card onto an IDBI card at 0.99% for 6 months, and show the interest saved and the effect on her utilisation ratio.

signals.title: Limit increase supported on banking conduct
signals.headline: ₹4.25L pre-approved, ₹6.00L on 6 months of conduct
signals.detail: The pre-approved figure is built from eight years of banking history, an average balance of ₹2.69L and a clean repayment record on ₹36.75L of borrowing — not from the thin card file the bureau sees. Once the card has run six clean cycles the limit review is automatic and lands near ₹6.00L.
signals.opportunity: Say the six-month step-up out loud at the point of sale. A customer choosing between three offers picks the one that tells them where it goes next.
signals.prompt: Draft what I should say to Vandana Singh about the ₹4.25L pre-approved card limit and the ₹6.00L review after six months of clean conduct.

signals.title: Score up 76 points, but the card file is thin
signals.headline: 690 in Mar 2025 → 766 today, on one card
signals.detail: The score recovered from a 654 dip in late 2024 after a stretched quarter, and has climbed steadily since the business stabilised. It is being carried almost entirely by the loan repayment record — one card since 2019 is a thin revolving file, which is why the score has stalled just under 770 despite everything else being clean.
signals.opportunity: A second card, used lightly and paid in full, widens the revolving file and typically adds 10–15 points over three to four cycles. Worth mentioning only as a reason, never as a promise.
signals.prompt: Explain in plain language how Vandana Singh's CIBIL score moved from 690 to 766 and why a thin card file is holding it under 770.

social.source: Public-profile probe · LinkedIn, Instagram, X · consent on file, 12 Jun 2026

posts.matched: Verified · name, location and business match
posts.text: Eight years ago this was a two-machine unit. Today Vandana Enterprises has been empanelled as a Tier-2 supplier to a leading auto OEM, and our Kila Raipur unit doubles capacity from October. To every supplier who said a woman-run shop could not hold tolerance — thank you for the motivation.
posts.signal: Capacity expansion with a committed OEM order book
posts.opportunity: An OEM empanelment is a receivable you can lend against. Doubling capacity from October means machinery spend now and a working-capital gap by November, which is the enquiry already sitting open on her file. The order book converts that from a judgement call into a documented one.
posts.prompt: Vandana Singh posted that Vandana Enterprises has been empanelled as a Tier-2 auto OEM supplier and doubles capacity from October. Assess what this means for her working-capital enquiry and what facilities to put in front of her.

posts.matched: Business handle linked from the LinkedIn profile
posts.text: New CNC line is in. Took eleven months of planning and one very long night of installation. Kila Raipur unit, September 2026.
posts.media: Four photographs of a newly installed CNC line on the shop floor
posts.signal: Capital asset acquired, financed outside IDBI
posts.opportunity: A CNC line of this class runs ₹18–24L and nothing of that size moved through her IDBI accounts, so it was financed elsewhere or paid from reserves. Either way the asset is new, probably uninsured, and her shop policy is already under-declared by ₹13L. This is the concrete example that makes the under-insurance conversation land.
posts.prompt: Vandana Singh installed a new CNC line in September 2026 that was not financed through IDBI. Assess the refinance and asset-insurance opportunity, and tie it to the ₹13L under-declaration on her shop policy.

posts.matched: Handle matches registered mobile; profile is partially private
posts.text: OEM payment cycles have stretched to 75 days. Every MSME founder I know is quietly financing someone else's working capital and calling it growth.
posts.opportunity: She has said the quiet part out loud: the receivable cycle has gone from roughly 45 days to 75. That is a ₹9–11L hole in her cycle at current turnover and it will widen when capacity doubles in October. Invoice discounting against OEM receivables prices better than an overdraft and does not need fresh collateral.
posts.prompt: Vandana Singh publicly said OEM payment cycles have stretched to 75 days. Size the receivables gap for Vandana Enterprises and compare invoice discounting against an overdraft enhancement.

posts.text: Speaking at the Ludhiana MSME Summit next month on women-led manufacturing and access to credit. If you are building in Punjab, come say hello.
posts.signal: Visible in the regional MSME network
posts.opportunity: Not a product signal — a relationship one. She is speaking on access to credit at a summit we sponsor, and she banks with us. A referral conversation costs nothing and she is standing in front of exactly the customers we want.
posts.prompt: Vandana Singh is speaking at the Ludhiana MSME Summit on women-led manufacturing and access to credit. Suggest how to use this as a relationship and referral touchpoint.
